name: Borgo Egnazia
positioning: Family-owned Puglian resort built to look like a village, where the Itria Valley hills meet the Adriatic, with private beaches, a spa and golf
best_for: Families wanting a drop-in kids' club and a child-friendly restaurant
Couples and travellers after a Puglian village setting near the sea

facts.text: Borgo Egnazia is in Savelletri di Fasano, where the hills of the Itria Valley fall away to the Adriatic Sea.
The property is inspired by the shapes, materials and colours of a typical Puglian village.
Borgo Egnazia is a family business of the Melpignanos, who also own nearby San Domenico.
Borgo Egnazia has been part of The Leading Hotels of the World since 2010.
The restaurants include La Frasca and Due Camini.
The spa has Roman baths, with fires lit in the cooler months.
San Domenico Golf is surrounded by ancient olive trees, with views that stretch to the sea.
A dedicated team called the Local Advisers is always available to guests.
Da Frisella serves help-yourself bowls of pasta and has plenty of colouring activities for children.
Staff take guests cycling, riding, or by tuk-tuk to nearby ruins for a picnic lunch.
Some villas have swimming pools or sea views from the rooftops.

highlights.text: The Puglian village feel was built entirely from scratch.
The hotel has two private beaches, Cala Masciola and La Fonte.
At the Cala Masciola beach club there are cushioned sun beds and lobsters in tanks to choose for lunch.
Homemade breakfasts are prepared by Puglian Massaie.
The drop-in kids' club includes cooking classes, puppet shows and trips to see the horses and donkeys at the farm.

considerations.text: Brindisi airport is about 50 km away, about 30 minutes by car; Bari airport is about 55 km away, about 45 minutes by car.
The nearest railway station is at Fasano, about 5 km from the hotel.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the luxury positioning.
